result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Baseline inspected all src/main sources/configuration plus Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example and oracle-init scripts; credential values are excluded from all report evidence. Runtime database/admin passwords are external required variables; example values are documented placeholders rather than active hard-coded credentials. BCrypt generates salts; no hard-coded crypto key found. Public gallery permissions are intentional and state-changing endpoints require authentication; database grants are schema-scoped without DBA. Static review only; runtime environment secrets, image/host permissions, TLS termination, operational audit infrastructure and historical git secrets were not inspected; no builds/tests.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: DetailController.deletePhoto logs successful destructive operations at lines 64-70 with only the photo ID, and PhotoServiceImpl.deletePhoto repeats an ID-only event at lines 191-204. Neither records the authenticated principal or request/source identity; no application MDC/audit interceptor supplying actor context was identified. Thus a security-critical deletion omits who performed the action even though SecurityConfig requires authentication. This finding concerns missing audit details in existing logs, not an unverified claim that Spring never logs authentication failures.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
